questions.q: Couldn't the low loss be validation text that also appears in training?
questions.a: Overlap would lower the loss at every position alike. A mask leak leaves the last position of each block at a normal loss, because its target is outside the block: in our tiny-Shakespeare run, 2.56 there against 0.003 elsewhere. So the per-position losses tell the two apart (our reasoning).

questions.q: Why does a NaN in one row matter so much?
questions.a: Anything multiplied or added with NaN is NaN, so one fully masked row with −inf scores makes that row's softmax output NaN, and the backward pass carries it into the gradients of shared weights. In our PyTorch 2.15 run, softmax over a row of −inf scores returned NaN in every entry.

questions.a: Only where the format can hold it, and only for rows that keep at least one allowed key: in our PyTorch 2.15 run, scores of 1, 2, −1e9, −1e9 gave weights 0.27, 0.73, 0, 0. A row with no allowed key spreads its weight evenly over keys meant to be hidden. fp16 can't hold −1e9 at all (its largest magnitude is 65,504), so it is stored as −inf; bf16, with float32's range, can.

questions.q: Why does a model with a leaking causal mask write nonsense even though its loss is tiny?
questions.a: In training it learned to copy the next token, which it could see. When generating, the next token doesn't exist yet, so the skill it learned has nothing to work on.

questions.q: Describe the one-edit test for a causal mask.
questions.a: Change only the last input token, rerun the forward pass, and check the outputs at every earlier position are unchanged. Any change means some position can see a later token.

questions.q: A boolean causal mask works with scaled_dot_product_attention but leaks in nn.MultiheadAttention. Why?
questions.a: The two read True oppositely: in scaled_dot_product_attention True means “may attend”, in nn.MultiheadAttention True means “blocked”. The same mask hides the past and shows the future.
